name: Lechi (Side Post for Alleyway)
notes: The side post used to render an alleyway fit for carrying on Shabbat; distinct from the cross beam (korah); rules about its minimum dimensions and construction

name: Korah (Cross Beam for Alleyway)
notes: The cross beam placed over the entrance of an alleyway to permit carrying; rules about its minimum width, strength, height, and material

name: Passei Biraot (Boards Around a Well)
notes: The rabbinic enactment permitting upright corner boards (deyomadin) arranged around a public well to create a virtual partition, enabling drawing water on Shabbat

name: Tzurat HaPetach (Form of a Doorway)
notes: Two vertical posts with a horizontal beam spanning them, serving as a valid halakhic partition or entrance marker for eruvin purposes

name: Mechitzot (Partitions for Shabbat Domains)
notes: The laws of valid partitions for creating Shabbat domains, including minimum height (10 handbreadths), construction from various materials, lavud principle, and breach rules

name: Eruv Techumin (Joining of Shabbat Boundaries)
notes: The eiruv that allows extension of the Shabbat limit by depositing food at a chosen location before Shabbat, establishing one's 'residence' there; distinct from eruv chatzeirot

name: Shituf Mevo'ot (Merging of Alleyways)
notes: The specific procedures, measures, and food requirements for merging courtyards that open into a shared alleyway; how it relates to eruv chatzeirot

name: Renunciation of Domain Rights (Bitul Reshut)
notes: The act by which a resident who forgot to participate in an eruv renounces his domain rights in the courtyard to allow the others to carry; rules about timing and effect

name: Measurement of Shabbat Limit (Middot Techum)
notes: The technical rules for measuring the 2000-cubit Shabbat limit: use of 50-cubit rope, treatment of hills and valleys, squaring the city, extending the city boundary (karpef)

name: City Boundary Extension for Shabbat (Tzurat HaIr)
notes: Rules for extending the outline of a city to include protrusions, turrets, and remnants of walls before measuring the Shabbat limit; squaring the city to gain corners

name: Karpef Addition to City Boundary
notes: The additional 70-cubit buffer added around every city before measuring the Shabbat limit; how this combines two adjacent towns into one for techum purposes

name: Shabbat Limit for One Taken Out Involuntarily
notes: Rules for one taken outside the Shabbat limit by gentiles or mental illness: whether he retains only 4 cubits or regains his original limit upon return

name: Acquisition of Shabbat Residence While Asleep or Unaware
notes: Dispute whether a sleeping or unaware person automatically acquires a Shabbat residence at his location or requires only 4 cubits (Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri vs. Rabbis)

name: Conditional Eruv (Eiruv Al Tenai)
notes: The ability to establish an eruv with a condition, choosing which direction the eruv will take effect based on circumstances; rules and limits of such conditions

name: Renting Domain from Gentile for Eruv
notes: The requirement to rent the rights of a gentile or non-observant resident in a shared courtyard in order to permit carrying there via eruv

name: Alleyway (Mavoy) — Eruv Laws
notes: The halakhic definition of a mavoy (alleyway), its structural requirements for carrying, and interaction between eruv chatzeirot and shituf mevo'ot

name: Gezuztra (Balcony) — Shabbat Domain
notes: Rules about balconies overhanging water or public domains and drawing water through holes on Shabbat; partition requirements for balconies

name: Drawing Water on Shabbat
notes: Specific rules governing drawing water from cisterns, channels, or wells on Shabbat, including partition requirements and domain considerations

name: Pouring Waste Water on Shabbat
notes: Laws about pouring waste water into a small courtyard or public domain on Shabbat; requirement for a pit, minimum courtyard size of 4 cubits

name: Carrying Between Domains (Transfer of Objects)
notes: Practical rules about a person standing in one domain and handling objects in another domain; positions of body and object relative to domain boundaries

name: Carrying Phylacteries on Shabbat
notes: Special rules for rescuing phylacteries found in the public domain on Shabbat by donning them pair by pair; passsing them hand-to-hand less than 4 cubits

name: Rescuing Sacred Writings on Shabbat
notes: Rules about rolling back a Torah scroll that fell into the public domain on Shabbat; priority of rescue of sacred writings over rabbinic Shabbat decrees

name: Rooftops as Shabbat Domain
notes: The dispute whether all roofs of a city form one shared domain or each is independent; rules about height differences between adjacent roofs

name: Breach in a Wall or Partition on Shabbat
notes: Rules about when a breach invalidates a partition: breaches up to 10 cubits treated as doorways; breaches over 10 cubits invalidating the domain

name: Temple Shabbat Leniencies (Miqdash vs. Medinah)
notes: Activities permitted in the Temple on Shabbat that are forbidden outside it due to rabbinic decree: closing bolts, removing impurity, tying harp strings, cutting warts, medical treatment of priests

name: Removing Creeping Animal Impurity from Temple on Shabbat
notes: The obligation and method for removing a sheretz (creeping creature) from the Temple precincts on Shabbat; dispute about which areas require removal

name: Lavud (Constructive Connection of Gaps)
notes: The halakhic principle that gaps of less than 3 handbreadths between surfaces are treated as closed/connected; applied to partitions in eruvin

name: Shabbat Residence in Courtyard (Shevisah b'Chatzar)
notes: The concept that a person's Shabbat residence is established in his home and courtyard, forming the basis for eruv chatzeirot; interaction between house, courtyard and alleyway domains

name: Two Days of Yom Tov — Eruv Considerations
notes: The dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbis about establishing separate eruvin for each of two consecutive days of Yom Tov or Yom Tov adjacent to Shabbat

name: Two Days of Rosh HaShanah — Eruv and Calendar Uncertainty
hebrew: שני ימי ראש השנה לעניין עירוב
notes: Rabbi Yehuda's view allowing separate eruvin for the two potentially-Rosh-HaShanah days due to calendar uncertainty; rabbinic disagreement; conditional tithing on Rosh HaShanah

name: Military Camp Exemptions (Machaneh Tzava)
notes: Four exemptions granted to soldiers in a military camp: wood gathering without concern for theft, handwashing before eating, separation of demai tithes, and eruv establishment

name: Deyomadin (Corner Posts Around a Well)
notes: The L-shaped double corner posts used in pairs to construct the virtual partition around a well; their minimum dimensions and spacing requirements
